issues.description: Method checkOrderReady: the problem statement's UML and textual specification declare checkOrderReady() with return type void (problem_statement.md line 32), but the reference solution implements checkOrderReady() with return type boolean (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 20). This mismatch can confuse students about the required method signature (whether a boolean must be returned and used) and lead to inconsistent implementations or mismatched tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API between specification and solution. Either (A) update the problem statement to allow/require public boolean checkOrderReady() and document the meaning of the boolean return value, or (B) change the solution to implement public void checkOrderReady() (remove the boolean return and adjust the method body to not return a value). Preferable student-facing fix: make checkOrderReady() void in the reference solution and update any callers/tests so the method signature matches the UML and textual description.
